style: Disciplined, counter-attacking side under Jamal Sellami that sits compact and breaks at pace through star forward Mousa Al-Tamari. Relies on defensive organization and dead balls; thin on top-five-league experience beyond their talisman.
recent_form: Qualified for their first-ever World Cup, capitalizing on the AFC's expanded allocation. Building up via friendlies (incl. an Austria test) but weakened by the loss of striker Yazan Al-Naimat to a knee injury.

key_players.name: Mousa Al-Tamari
key_players.note: Rennes forward and the only squad member in a top-five European league; 24 goals in 91 caps and the team's creative and goal threat.

key_players.name: Ali Olwan
key_players.note: Third-highest scorer across all AFC qualifying rounds with nine goals; returns from injury to lead the line.

key_players.name: Yazan Al-Arab
key_players.note: Defensive leader anchoring Jordan's compact back line.

key_players.name: Nour Al-Rawabdeh
key_players.note: Energetic midfielder contributing in transition and out of possession.

key_players.name: Yazeed Abulaila
key_players.note: First-choice keeper expected to be heavily tested as underdogs.

historical_news: Qualified for their first-ever World Cup, taking advantage of the AFC's expanded eight direct slots.
Star forward Mousa Al-Tamari headlines coach Jamal Sellami's 26-man squad.
Influential striker Yazan Al-Naimat ruled out after a knee injury at the FIFA Arab Cup.
Reached a maiden Asian Cup final in 2024, signaling the federation's rise before this World Cup.
Drawn into a daunting Group J with Austria, Algeria and reigning champions Argentina.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Historic, celebratory mood around a debut World Cup appearance, with hopes resting heavily on Al-Tamari; realistic acknowledgment of underdog status in a brutal group and the blow of losing Al-Naimat.
